items.stem: What is actual economic growth?
options: An increase in the price level
items.answer: An increase in real GDP
items.markingKey: Measured as % change in real GDP.

items.stem: Explain the difference between actual and potential economic growth.
items.answer: Actual growth is an increase in real output (using more resources or idle capacity); potential growth is an increase in productive capacity (more/better resources, technology), shown by an outward shift of the PPC or LRAS.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Explain why actual growth cannot exceed potential growth for long.
items.answer: Once spare capacity is used up, output can only rise as fast as capacity grows; trying to grow faster causes inflation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: capacity limit; 1 mark: inflation [2]

items.stem: Nordavia: Year: 1, 2, 3, 4; Real GDP ($ billion): 400, 416, 428.5, 449.9. Calculate the growth rate of real GDP in Year 3.
Zentara: Year: 1, 2, 3, 4; Real GDP ($ billion): 400, 420, 415.8, 420. (a) Calculate the growth rate in each of Years 2 to 4 and over the whole period. (b) Comment on the performance of the economy.
items.answer: (a) +5%, −1%, +1%; overall +5%. (b) Output fell in at least one year, suggesting a slowdown or recession; growth was uneven, and per capita and distribution data would be needed to judge living standards.
items.markingKey: (a) three annual rates [2]; overall [1] (b) comment using data [1] [4]

items.stem: Extract: Annual growth of real GDP in Umbria Nova over five years was 3.5%, 2%, −1%, −0.3% and 1.5%. The output gap is now estimated at −3% of potential GDP. The government plans to raise spending on infrastructure and training. Environmental groups warn that a return to rapid growth will increase pollution. (a) Identify the phases of the economic cycle shown by the data. (b) Explain one cost of economic growth mentioned in the extract.
items.answer: (a) Boom/slowdown (years 1–2), recession (years 3–4), recovery (year 5). (b) Pollution: negative externality, health costs, not measured in GDP.
items.markingKey: (a) Credit: Boom/slowdown (years 1–2), recession (years 3–4), recovery (year 5). [2] (b) Credit: Pollution: negative externality, health costs, not measured in GDP. [2]

items.stem: Real GDP in Istrana grew by 6% last year while unemployment fell sharply. Explain whether this was mainly actual or potential growth.
items.answer: Mainly actual growth: idle resources (unemployed workers) were brought into use, moving towards the PPC.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: actual; 1 mark: idle resources used [2]

items.stem: Real GDP in Pelora grew by 6% last year while unemployment fell sharply. Explain whether this was mainly actual or potential growth.
items.answer: Mainly actual growth: idle resources (unemployed workers) were brought into use, moving towards the PPC.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: actual; 1 mark: idle resources used [2]

items.stem: Newspapers in Zentara have recently reported a lively debate among economists on this issue. Explain the difference between actual and potential economic growth, using diagrams.
items.answer: Actual: rise in real GDP, movement towards PPC/AD shift with spare capacity; potential: capacity, PPC/LRAS shift; measurement with real GDP.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: Actual: rise in real GDP, movement towards PPC/AD shift with spare capacity; potential: capacity, PPC/LRAS shift; measurement with real GDP. items.stem: Extract: Annual growth of real GDP in Jovania over five years was 3.5%, 1.5%, −0.5%, −0.3% and 1%. The output gap is now estimated at −3% of potential GDP. The government plans to raise spending on infrastructure and training. Environmental groups warn that a return to rapid growth will increase pollution. (a) Explain how infrastructure and training spending could lead to both actual and potential growth. (b) Explain one cost of economic growth mentioned in the extract.
items.answer: (a) Raises AD now (using spare capacity) and LRAS later (productivity). (b) Pollution: negative externality, health costs, not measured in GDP.
items.markingKey: (a) Credit: Raises AD now (using spare capacity) and LRAS later (productivity). [3] (b) Credit: Pollution: negative externality, health costs, not measured in GDP. [2]

items.stem: Which is a cause of long-run economic growth?
options: Investment in new capital and technology
A rise in the price level
items.answer: Investment in new capital and technology
items.markingKey: Increases productive capacity.

items.stem: Explain two causes of potential economic growth.
items.answer: More capital (investment); better technology; more labour (population, migration, participation); better quality labour (education, health); discovery of resources; better institutions.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each cause, 1 mark each explained [4]

items.stem: Explain how an increase in investment can lead to both actual and potential growth.
items.answer: Investment spending raises AD now (actual growth if there is spare capacity) and adds to the capital stock, raising LRAS (potential growth).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: AD; 1 mark: LRAS [2]

items.stem: Households in Fendaria increase spending after a tax cut while unemployment is high. What type of growth does this mainly cause?
items.answer: Actual growth (AD-led)
items.markingKey: Actual growth (AD-led): spare capacity is used as AD rises.

items.stem: What is a common definition of a recession?
options: Two consecutive quarters of falling real GDP
A fall in the price level
A rise in unemployment for one month
items.answer: Two consecutive quarters of falling real GDP
items.markingKey: Negative growth for two quarters.

items.stem: Explain the difference between a positive and a negative output gap.
items.answer: Positive: actual output above potential (resources over-used, inflationary pressure). Negative: actual below potential (spare capacity, unemployment, low inflation).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Explain the main phases of the economic cycle.
items.answer: Recovery (growth resumes), boom (rapid growth, inflation, positive gap), slowdown/downturn, recession (falling output, unemployment, negative gap).
items.markingKey: 1 mark per two phases correctly described [3]

items.answer: Quarters 3 and 4
items.markingKey: Negative quarters: [1, 3, 4, 5]; consecutive pair → Quarters 3 and 4.

items.stem: Jovania: Quarter: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; Growth of real GDP (%): −0.4, 0.9, 0.4, 0.1, 0.6, −1.2. Potential output is $1000bn and actual output is $960bn. (a) Identify whether there was a recession in the data. (b) Calculate the output gap as a percentage of potential output and state whether it is positive or negative. (c) Explain one likely consequence of this output gap.
items.answer: (a) No: there were no two consecutive quarters of negative growth. (b) −4% (negative). (c) Unemployment and low inflation; lost output.

The government plans to raise spending on infrastructure and training. Environmental groups warn that a return to rapid growth will increase pollution. (a) Explain how infrastructure and training spending could lead to both actual and potential growth. (b) Discuss whether the benefits of a return to rapid growth would outweigh the costs.
items.answer: (a) Raises AD now (using spare capacity) and LRAS later (productivity). (b) Jobs, incomes, tax revenue vs pollution, inequality, inflation risk once gap closes; green growth possible; judgement.
items.markingKey: (a) Credit: Raises AD now (using spare capacity) and LRAS later (productivity). [3] (b) Credit: Jobs, incomes, tax revenue vs pollution, inequality, inflation risk once gap closes; green growth possible; judgement. [5]

items.stem: In a revision note Elena wrote: ‘Economic growth always benefits everyone in the economy.’ Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: Gains may be unevenly distributed and growth can impose costs such as pollution, congestion and structural unemployment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error; 1 mark: correct explanation – Gains may be unevenly distributed and growth can impose costs such as pollution, congestion and structural unemployment. [2]

items.stem: Unemployment in Marvona fell from 9% to 5% during a period of rapid growth, but house prices in Riyadh doubled. Explain one benefit and one cost of the growth for households.
items.answer: Benefit: more jobs and higher incomes as unemployment fell 4 percentage points. Cost: housing became much less affordable, especially for young and low-income households.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each with data, 1 mark development [3]

items.stem: Extract: Annual growth of real GDP in Valdoria over five years was 4.5%, 1.5%, −0.5%, −0.3% and 1%. The output gap is now estimated at −3% of potential GDP. The government plans to raise spending on infrastructure and training. Environmental groups warn that a return to rapid growth will increase pollution. (a) Identify the phases of the economic cycle shown by the data. (b) Explain how infrastructure and training spending could lead to both actual and potential growth.
items.answer: (a) Boom/slowdown (years 1–2), recession (years 3–4), recovery (year 5). (b) Raises AD now (using spare capacity) and LRAS later (productivity).
